title: seamless run / speed walk on phone and laptop (double-tap and hold), in both venues
lensAText: a sceptical mobile game UX lead and animator. Look at the builder's frames with the Read tool, then build dist/artifact.html yourself and take your own frames in ONE short Playwright script (keyboard and touch events): in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (Go To, Get out) at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, isMobile, hasTouch, DPR 3) and 1280x720: on the laptop, does a single W press walk and a double-tap-and-hold of W (and Shift) run, and does releasing return to walk; on the phone, does double-tap-and-hold on the stick and an edge push run; is it seamless (the walk blends into the run with no pop or stutter in first and third person), is the stick's run cue sleek and clear, is the one-time hint there, are the controls uncluttered; do collisions, crowds, stairs (walk), indoors (speed walk) and tap-to-go still behave?
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-12 ~5:28 PM PT): "lets make a running button for both the laptop and phone so it should be seamless". TODAY (read src/onfoot/lot57/input.ts and player.ts, and the sports bar's own venues/sportsbar/player.ts and main.ts): on foot the player walks at 1.4 m/s and jogs at 3.0 m/s, only outdoors (player.ts: 'run && !this.indoors'); jog is reached by Shift on a keyboard or by pushing the touch stick past 92 %; there is NO visible run control, so players don't know running exists. BUILD, in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time, both inside the game (src/onfoot/embed.ts mount) and on the standalone pages: (1) SEAMLESS RUN, NO EXTRA BUTTON TO HUNT FOR (the owner refined it, 2026-11-15 ~2:15 PM PT: "just make it run / speed walk seamlessly for both devices so maybe for computer it comes with just double tapping and holding the up button, etc."). Computer: DOUBLE-TAP AND HOLD forward (W or the Up arrow) to run, like a sprint: a second press within about 300 ms of the first starts running and it lasts while the key is held (diagonals with A/D keep running; releasing W returns to walk); Shift held still runs too. Phone: the same idea on the left stick: DOUBLE-TAP AND HOLD where the stick floats to run straight away, and pushing the stick out to its edge also runs; easing back or lifting returns to walk. Show the state on the stick itself (a sleek accent glow on the stick ring and a small 'RUN' tag), in the same visual language as the driving touch controls; no separate big button (the owner asked to keep controls uncluttered); a one-time hint chip teaches it ('Double-tap and hold W to run' on a computer, 'Double-tap and hold to run' on a phone). Gamepad: a full stick push runs, L3 click toggles run. (2) Seamless: walk to run and back with smooth acceleration (about 0.3 s up, 0.2 s down), the walk cycle blending into the existing jog/run gait the people builder already has (the NPC jogger uses it) with no pop, a slight camera bob and FOV ease in first person, the third-person camera keeping up without lag; stopping is crisp. A real run speed (about 4.5 m/s outdoors); indoors a speed walk (about 2.6 m/s) instead of none, and no running through crowds (slow to walk near people and on stairs); the existing collision, pathing (tap to go stays walking) and occlusion keep working. (3) Honest and cheap: no stamina system unless trivial (none is required); no per-frame allocation; phone-cheap; reduced motion: no bob or FOV change. Do NOT edit src/onfoot/people/* (another lane rebuilds the characters there; use the gait the builder already exposes; if a parameter you need is missing, say so instead), src/preview/hands*, spec.ts, car-wheel.ts or Physics.ts. ADD regression checks (both venues: a single W press walks, double-tap-and-hold W runs and Shift runs, the phone stick's double-tap-and-hold and edge push run, outdoors at the run speed and indoors at the speed-walk speed, releasing returns to walk within 0.3 s, the stick's run cue shows, the gait switches without a frame where the mesh pops). PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (one owner-test mark); npm test -- --only=boot,venues and the new checks; the standalone venue builds (npx vite build --config src/onfoot/vite.config.ts and --config src/onfoot/vite.sportsbar.config.ts); frames: the phone layout (390x844 phone viewport copy, DPR 3) with the stick idle and in its run state, and the laptop (1280x720) with the one-time hint, in both venues, plus a 6-frame strip of the walk-to-run transition in third person. Log it in PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md and the venues' own docs.
